prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the floor and nearby people from the darker, farther wall: the floor immediately below the camera is closest, while the wall and entrance are roughly 5–10 m ahead. In each frame, several people occupy the middle distance, mostly about 2–6 m from the camera and roughly 1–4 m apart; the nearest figures lie toward the left edge in frame 1 and the right edge in frame 5, where they are partly out of view. Across the five frames, changing silhouettes and brightness suggest the camera turns right, causing people to shift leftward through the view, while a few foreground figures appear nearer or farther as their size changes. This map makes distance ordering and silhouette occlusion clearer than RGB, but its smooth floor gradient, merged neighboring people, missing object detail, and inconsistent boundary depths make exact metre estimates and inter-person distances unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies many separate person instances across the concourse, plus a small skateboard-like object at the lower-left edge of frame 1; most other scene structures and objects are left black. It clarifies which overlapping silhouettes are distinct people, including clusters approximately 2–5 m ahead whose members stand about 0.3–2 m apart, and it shows people cropped at the left edge of frame 1 and right edge of frame 5. Across the sequence, the same general groups shift left as the camera turns right, while nearer figures expand or leave the frame and more people enter from the right; relative left/right placement is clear, but front/behind ordering must be inferred from mask overlap and RGB scale. The masks are unreliable where bodies overlap or are small: some limbs are truncated, labels collide, one figure appears fragmented, and the skateboard label near the border may be a false or partial detection.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates a single prominent body skeleton in each frame, corresponding approximately to the nearer central person in the RGB, and shows joint locations, body orientation, and limb configuration more clearly than RGB. The detected person moves from the left side in frame 1 to right-of-center in frame 5 as the camera pans, remaining roughly 2–4 m away and therefore outside the camera wearer's arm reach; nearby people generally appear about 0.5–2 m from that person, although they lack skeletons. The torso and head orientation suggest the person is mostly side-on or angled away rather than directly facing the camera, with posture changing from bent/leaning in frame 1 to more upright later; the sparse frame-4 skeleton makes its facing direction uncertain. No magenta hand skeletons are visible, and missed people, incomplete joints, distorted limbs, and the tiny fragmentary detection in frame 4 make reach, gaze, occlusion, and above/below relationships unreliable for anyone except the one detected body.
